title: Detect and sweep TTL-replayed keys causing memory leak and eviction anomalies
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: During a capacity event in Nov 2025 we observed the prefix/KV cache memory footprint growing for some hosts despite steady eviction rates. Heap snapshots and request-trace correlation show keys being 'replayed' — TTLs updated non-atomically after eviction decisions resulting in resurrection of keys that should have been removed, causing effective memory leak and eviction thrashing. This ticket tracks detection, automated sweep remediation, and long-term fixes (atomic TTL updates + testing).
reproduction_steps: 1) Synthetic load: concurrent cold-writes + background prefix prefetch enabled
2) Configure short TTLs (2s) and aggressive eviction policy on test pool
3) Pump a pattern of requests which first evict then re-issue a set of keys within the TTL update window
4) Observe: cache size grows, eviction cycles increase, heap snapshots show nodes with resurrected stamp values
investigation_notes: Telemetry: increased 'cache_insert' + 'eviction' churn with net positive growth on affected hosts; flamegraphs showed GC pressure centered in slab allocator
Heap snapshots: retained objects tied to prefix entries with unexpected reference counts; tombstone markers intermittently present

Race: identified code path where TTL extension is performed without owning the eviction lock; if eviction decides to remove key concurrently, the subsequent TTL update can re-add entry to active index without updating tombstone, causing 'phantom' live entries
Reproducible in local integration harness with deterministic scheduling (record/replay) when scheduling delays introduced between eviction decision and TTL update callback
Impacted stack: prefix cache index + background prefetch + KV client retry logic where retransmits can cause duplicated insertion flow

action_items: A1: Add deterministic metric 'ttl_replay_rate' and trace tags for replayed keys (owner: Diego) - in progress
A2: Implement atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) for TTL updates on prefix entries to avoid resurrection race (owner: Platform Caching team) - PR opened
A3: Build background sweeper process that scans prefix index for invalid tombstone/TTL states and evicts/resolves with checkpointed progress and rate-limiting (owner: Diego) - design approved
A4: Add integration test harness scenario for TTL-race with deterministic scheduler and include in CI smoke runs (owner: TestInfra) - blocked on harness infra upgrade
A5: Dashboard: surface 'ttl_replay_rate', per-host memory delta, eviction_thrash_ratio; set alert for >0.5% sustained replay rate (owner: Observability) - in progress
A6: Backfill remediation: run sweeper once cluster-wide in maintenance windows for hosts with replay rate > threshold; publish runbook (owner: SRE) - planned
A7: Post-deploy: 7-day monitoring window and run regression prompts against known promptsets to ensure quality not impacted by CAS/ejection changes (owner: Applied ML) - planned
